question.worked_solution:
First, we clear the rational expressions by multiplying both sides of the inequality by the lowest common positive multiple of the denominators:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3z+1}{2} & >\frac{-28+6z}{7} \\ 14\cdot (\frac{3z+1}{2}) & >14\cdot (\frac{-28+6z}{7}) \\ 7\cdot (3z+1) & >2\cdot (-28+6z) \\ 21z+7 & >-56+12z\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}21z+7 & >-56+12z \\ 21z+7-12z & >-56+12z-12z \\ 9z+7 & >-56 \\ 9z+7-7 & >-56-7 \\ 9z & >-63 \\ \frac{9z}{9} & >\frac{-63}{9} \\ z & >-7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $z>-7.$
